sections.h2: Who records property documents in Otsego County, Michigan?
sections.html:
The Otsego County Register of Deeds is in Gaylord at 225 W Main Street, Gaylord, MI 49735. The main line is 989-731-7550 and the fax is 989-731-7519. The county describes the office as keeper of every record that transfers or encumbers real estate in the county.

Each document is recorded, time stamped, given liber and page numbers and indexed on computer. The computerized index and images start on March 5, 1864, and every record can be pulled and copied in the office within minutes. Images are also sold online.

The office works with the county Equalization Department to keep ownership current, using tax identification numbers or owner names. It does not run searches for the public. A buyer or seller who wants a search done for them should call a title insurance company or a land records data company, or come in and search at the counter.

sections.h2: What does the Otsego County Register of Deeds charge?
sections.html:
Recording costs $30 per document, with all pages included. The county page dates that rate to October 1, 2016. The table below comes straight from the county's fee and copies pages.

Otsego County Register of Deeds fees, from otsegocountymi.gov
ServiceFee
Recording a document, all pages$30
Each extra instrument a document assigns or discharges$3
Copies of recorded instruments$1 per page
Certification of a document$5
Real estate record search$5 per name
State or federal tax lien certificate$3 per name
U.C.C.-11 certificate$6 per name

The county notes that $4 of the recording fee goes to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation Fund. That share is not collected on fixture filings, state liens, federal liens, MESC liens, state deeds or plats. Mail orders for copies should be preceded by a call, because staff want to confirm the page count and the exact cost, and payment is due when the service is rendered. Checks go to Otsego County Register of Deeds.

sections.h2: How do transfer tax and exemptions work in Otsego County?
sections.html:
Transfer tax is collected when the deed is recorded, under MCL 207.505(5) and MCL 207.526(6) as the county's page cites them. The deed has to carry the total consideration on its face, or a real estate transfer valuation affidavit must be filed, and the county charges nothing to file that affidavit. If a transfer is exempt from one or both acts, the exemption has to be written on the face of the instrument.

The rates are $3.75 for the state and 55 cents for the county per $500 or fraction. They come from MCL 207.525 and MCL 207.504. A sale at $220,000, close to Otsego County's median owner-occupied value of $219,700, is 440 blocks of $500. State tax is $1,650 and county tax is $242, so $1,892 is due at recording unless an exemption applies.

These exemptions matter most to people selling or passing on a home:

  • Consideration below $100 removes the tax under both acts.
  • A deed from a foreclosure on a mortgage is exempt from the state tax, and one given on a government-backed loan is exempt from both. The state exemption does not carry over to the lender's later sale of the property.
  • A parent-to-child or grandparent-to-grandchild deed is exempt from the state tax only.
  • A land contract is exempt until the buyer has paid the full price and legal title passes.
  • A deed that moves a boundary line with no money paid is exempt from both.

Mineral rights transfers and leases are exempt too, but they come up rarely in a house sale.

sections.h2: Can I e-record or search Otsego County land records online?
sections.html:
Yes. Otsego County offers electronic recording for people who file many documents at once. It is a secure, verified-user service, and you register through an approved provider before you start. The county names Simplifile, at simplifile.com, and CSC, at cscglobal.com/service/erecording.

Online, the office sells images of recorded documents. Searching the real estate record at the office costs $5 per name, and certificate searches for state tax liens, federal tax liens and U.C.C.-11 filings carry the per-name fees in the table above.

Freedom of Information requests go on a completed FOIA Request Form sent by email to the county's FOIA coordinator or faxed to 989-731-7529. A deed copy does not need a FOIA request, since recorded instruments are available at $1 per page.

sections.h2: What paperwork should a deed carry before it reaches the Gaylord counter?
sections.html:
Two statutes decide whether the register will take a deed. MCL 565.201 covers the physical document, and MCL 211.135 covers tax proof. Gather both before you hand anything over, because the register may refuse an instrument that falls short.

  • Legible black or dark blue signatures, with each signer's name printed below and matching the notary's wording.
  • A printed grantee address and the name and business address of the person who drafted the instrument.
  • Black type of at least 10 points on white 20-pound paper, between letter and legal size, with a first-page top margin of 2.5 inches.
  • One line at the top of the first page naming the single recordable event, such as a warranty deed or a mortgage discharge.
  • Social Security numbers cut to the last four digits or fewer unless a law requires more.

For a deed that carries a covenant of warranty, the county treasurer certifies that no tax liens or titles are held against the parcel and that taxes for the five prior years are paid. A city, village or township treasurer certifies the local side. A quitclaim deed without warranty covenants, a sheriff's deed and a court-ordered conveyance are excused. In Otsego County, a lake property in Elmira or Johannesburg is certified through the same county office as a house in Gaylord.

sections.h2: What should I know about selling a house in Otsego County?
sections.html:
Otsego County covers 526 square miles in Northern Michigan and is the fifth-smallest county by total area. Gaylord is the county seat and the only city, and Vanderbilt is the lone village. Unincorporated communities include Elmira, Johannesburg, Waters, Sparr and the lakeside settlement of Otsego Lake. The county began as Okkuddo County in 1840, became Otsego in 1843, and organized in 1875.

Water shapes the housing stock. The county has more than 370 lakes, mostly in the south, and Otsego Lake is the largest at 1,972 acres. The headwaters of the Au Sable, Black, Manistee, Pigeon and Sturgeon rivers are here. I-75 bypasses Gaylord on the west and M-32 runs east and west through it.

The Census Bureau counted 25,091 residents in 2020 and estimates 26,080 for 2025, a 3.9% gain. For 2020 to 2024 it lists a median owner-occupied value of $219,700, an owner-occupied rate of 77.2% and median gross rent of $1,008. Median household income is $68,183. The county has 14,976 housing units but 11,231 households, so housing units outnumber households by about 3,700. Building permits numbered 25 in 2025, and retail sales per resident in 2022 were $39,474, far above the other three counties in the same release.

Owners of lake or woodland parcels should ask the Equalization Department for the parcel's tax identification number and the Treasurer for the tax certificate before they set a closing date.

faqs.q: What is the Otsego County recording fee?
faqs.a: It is $30 per document regardless of page count, plus $3 for each additional instrument a single document assigns or discharges, as shown on the county's Register of Deeds page.

faqs.q: Does Otsego County charge a fee to file the transfer valuation affidavit?
faqs.a: No. The county states that no fee is collected for filing the real estate transfer valuation affidavit, which you can use instead of printing the value on the deed.

faqs.q: How far back do Otsego County's computer records go?
faqs.a: They start on March 5, 1864. The office keeps both the index and the images on computer from that date to the present.

faqs.q: How much are copies from the Otsego County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Copies cost $1 per page, and certifying a document adds $5. Mail requests should be confirmed by phone first so staff can quote the exact total.

faqs.q: Does Otsego County search titles for sellers?
faqs.a: No. The office says search services are not provided, and it points people to a title insurance company or a land records data company. You can search the records in person at the Gaylord office.
